sentences.text: This pterosaur lived during the early Campanian stage of the Upper Cretaceous in the Rybushka Formation of Petrovsk, Saratov Oblast, Russia.
The genus was named after Nikolai Nikolaevich Bogolubov, who discovered the remains in 1914.
The original specimen, which consisted of a single partial large cervical vertebra, was initially assigned to the species Ornithostoma orientalis.
The species was later reclassified as Pteranodon before being moved to its own genus within the family Pteranodontidae by Nessov and Yarkov in 1989.
In 1991, the genus was assigned to the family Azhdarchidae, though Wellnhofer retained it as a Pteranodontidae.
New remains described in 2022 suggested that both Bogolubovia and Volgadraco are valid species of pteranodontids.
In 2008, some researchers considered Bogolubovia a nomen dubium that might be identical to the genus Volgadraco.
In 2020, Averianov and Arkhangelsky suggested that Bogolubovia is likely a valid pteranodontid based on similarities to Volgadraco.
